clue.text: Deals — that is, provided wind returns

indicators.note: returns means the whole string built from the three pieces is read backwards

parts.note: SC is short for scilicet, Latin for 'that is to say'
if means provided, as in 'if it rains'
fart is a crude word for breaking wind

explanation.surface: A shady negotiator agrees to deals only if someone's flatulence comes back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' turns SCIFFART round. SC is the dictionary abbreviation of scilicet, 'that is'.
explanation.definitionFit: To traffic is to deal or trade, often illicitly, so 'deals' is a verb synonym.

clue.text: Doctor once has place to bury ace, king and queen

parts.note: a tomb is a place to bury the dead
A is the card abbreviation for ace
K is the chess and card abbreviation for king
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A former doctor has a burial plot reserved for three playing cards.
explanation.walkthrough: The Doctor here is Doctor Who; Tom Baker played the fourth Doctor in the 1970s, hence 'once'.
explanation.definitionFit: Tom Baker is the actor who played Doctor Who from 1974 to 1981, a former holder of the role.

clue.text: After 40 winks, beg May not to start plan to repel doctors

parts.note: forty winks is a short sleep, a nap
to plead is to beg

indicators.note: not to start means the opening letter of May is dropped

explanation.surface: After a snooze, someone begs May not to begin a scheme against doctors.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb 'an apple a day keeps the doctor away' is the plan. 'After' just orders the pieces as they fall.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb recommends a daily fruit as a way of never needing a physician, a scheme for keeping medics at bay.

clue.text: Doctor from Australia complimentary about staff with tasteful clothes

indicators.note: about means the word for complimentary wraps around the other pieces

parts.note: complimentary means free of charge
to man is to staff, as in manning a desk

indicators.note: clothes signals the outer letters of tasteful, which clothe the rest

explanation.surface: An Australian doctor, generous about staff, wears tasteful clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clothes' takes T and L, the outside of 'tasteful'. The Fremantle Doctor is the cooling afternoon sea breeze that blows into Perth, Western Australia.
explanation.definitionFit: The local name for Perth's afternoon sea breeze is the Fremantle Doctor, a weather term from Western Australia.

clue.text: Bird needs metal cap to meet exacting standards

indicators.note: cap means the metal symbol sits on top of the bird in this down entry

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper, a metal
a tit is a small songbird

explanation.surface: A bird must wear a metal cap to pass muster.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer 'cap' puts CU above TIT.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut it is an idiom for being good enough, reaching the required level.

clue.text: In the Middle East, doctor stuffs excellent bird

indicators.note: In places what follows inside the abbreviation for the Middle East

parts.note: ME is the abbreviation for the Middle East

indicators.note: stuffs means the doctor goes inside the word for excellent

parts.note: A1 means excellent, written AI with letters
GP is a general practitioner, a family doctor

explanation.surface: A cook in the Middle East with a doctor fills a fine bird with stuffing.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 is written AI, the figure 1 standing as letter I. GP goes into AI, and AGPI goes into ME.
explanation.definitionFit: The magpie is a black-and-white crow-family species, so it is an example of a feathered creature.

clue.text: Given order to support a team

indicators.note: to support means the order abbreviation goes underneath in this down entry

parts.note: XI is eleven, a cricket or football team
OM is the Order of Merit

explanation.surface: Someone was told to back a team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Given' is a noun here: a premise taken for granted. The Order of Merit is a British honour, abbreviated OM.
explanation.definitionFit: A self-evident truth accepted without proof is called a given, a premise to reason from.

clue.text: Place sheep upside-down

indicators.note: upside-down in a down entry means the word for sheep is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a tup is a ram, a male sheep

explanation.surface: Someone puts a sheep upside-down.
explanation.definitionFit: To place something is to set it down, a direct verb synonym.

clue.text: Say "See about poem"

indicators.note: about means the cathedral see goes round the abbreviation for say

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city, a bishop's see
eg (for example) can stand for say, as in 'say, a dog'

explanation.surface: An instruction to look over a poem.
explanation.walkthrough: A see is a bishop's diocese; Ely in Cambridgeshire is the usual crossword one.
explanation.definitionFit: A mournful poem lamenting the dead is a specific kind of verse.

clue.text: Steely quality of daughter in control

indicators.note: in places the daughter abbreviation inside the word for control

parts.note: to harness is to control, as in harnessing energy
D is the genealogical abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A daughter shows a steely firmness when in charge.
explanation.definitionFit: Steel's toughness is a property of being hard, so a steely quality is firmness.

clue.text: Least likely to give false name with odd parts of website missing

indicators.note: false means the letters of name are presented in a fake order
with odd parts of the word missing, only its even letters survive
missing tells us the odd-placed letters of website go

explanation.surface: The stingiest person gives a false name, with half a website gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'false' shuffles NAME into MEAN; 'odd parts of website missing' keeps the 2nd, 4th and 6th letters, E, S, T.
explanation.definitionFit: The stingiest person is the least generous, the superlative of a miserly adjective.

clue.text: Some beer will control awful tilt

indicators.note: will control suggests holding something in, so the beer surrounds the rest

parts.note: ale is a type of beer

indicators.note: awful signals the letters of tilt are badly jumbled

explanation.surface: Drinking beer will correct a terrible lean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' is the definition, not a selection signal; the surface reads it as 'some beer'.
explanation.definitionFit: A small amount means some, as in 'have a bit'; the two-word phrase is a quantity adverb.

clue.text: Snake stopped covered road?

parts.note: an asp is a venomous snake
halted means stopped

explanation.surface: A snake brought traffic to a halt on a surfaced road.
explanation.definitionFit: Laying tarmac on a road surface is a way of covering it, hence the question mark for a definition by example.

clue.text: Medal given to shy space doctor

parts.note: MC is the Military Cross, a British gallantry medal
coy means bashful or shy

explanation.surface: A shy doctor in space receives a medal.
explanation.walkthrough: The Military Cross is a British gallantry decoration, abbreviated MC.
explanation.definitionFit: Dr Leonard 'Bones' McCoy is the ship's medic in Star Trek, a doctor among the stars.

clue.text: One making arrangements for new doctor on air

indicators.note: new means the letters are rearranged into a fresh form

explanation.surface: Someone organises a new doctor for a broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges all eleven letters of DOCTOR ON AIR.
explanation.definitionFit: An organiser who arranges and harmonises activities is someone making arrangements.

clue.text: Happening, even though 50% has gone missing

indicators.note: with half the phrase gone missing, only its first five of ten letters remain

explanation.surface: Something happens, even though half has disappeared.
explanation.walkthrough: EVENTHOUGH has ten letters; the first five stay.
explanation.definitionFit: An occurrence or incident is something that happens, a noun synonym.

clue.text: Doctor of music rewrites Log 24

indicators.note: rewrites means the combined letters are written out in a new order

parts.note: 24 points to the answer of 24 down, the novelist

explanation.surface: A doctor of music revises a ship's log.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rewrites' rearranges LOG plus DEFOE, the writer at 24 down. Dr Feelgood is a British pub-rock band from Canvey Island.
explanation.definitionFit: Dr Feelgood is the name of a band, so a doctor in the world of music.

clue.text: French spy keeps mobile bit

indicators.note: keeps means the spy holds the mobile abbreviation inside

parts.note: an agent is a spy
M marks a mobile phone number on business cards

explanation.surface: A French spy holds on to a mobile piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A fragment is a small piece broken off something, so a bit.

clue.text: Sue possibly understood round playing area

parts.note: got means understood, as in 'I got it'
O is round in shape
a court is an area for tennis or basketball

explanation.surface: Sue may have gathered there was a round playing area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sue' looks like a woman's name; it is the verb, to take legal action.
explanation.definitionFit: Suing someone is one way of taking a matter to law, hence 'possibly'.

clue.text: Healthy doctor sued, being in common operation

parts.note: well means in good health

indicators.note: to doctor is to alter or tamper, so the letters of sued are rearranged

explanation.surface: A fit doctor was sued while busy with routine work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doctor' is a verb, rearranging SUED.
explanation.definitionFit: Something worn from frequent handling is in common operation, much employed.

clue.text: Side has mass said in an unusual direction

parts.note: an edge is a side

indicators.note: said signals a word that sounds like the phrase before it

parts.note: something that has mass weighs something

explanation.surface: One side holds mass, said to point in an odd direction.
explanation.definitionFit: Moving sideways, edge first, is an unusual way to go.

clue.text: Editor not right about what subject of obituary has

indicators.note: about is used as a signal that the remaining letters are moved around
not means the right abbreviation is removed

explanation.surface: An editor, wrong about an obituary's subject.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not right' leaves EDITO, and 'about' rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: The subject of an obituary had, inevitably, to die: the phrase completes the clue as a sentence.

clue.text: Nymph doctor some time back

indicators.note: back means the word for some time reads backwards

parts.note: a day is a period of time

explanation.surface: A nymph saw a doctor some time ago.
explanation.definitionFit: A dryad is a tree spirit of Greek myth, a kind of nymph.

clue.text: Row as Simpson possibly turns up in French city

indicators.note: in puts the reversed name inside the word for row

parts.note: a din is a noisy row

indicators.note: turns up in a down entry means the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: O.J. Simpson is known as OJ; 'possibly' marks him as one example

explanation.surface: A fuss as some Simpson appears in a French city.
explanation.definitionFit: Dijon is the Burgundy capital in eastern France, famous for mustard.

clue.text: Some circles debate excluding America

indicators.note: excluding means the abbreviation for America is taken out

parts.note: to discuss is to debate
US is the United States

explanation.surface: Some groups debate leaving America out.
explanation.definitionFit: Discs are flat round shapes, so they are a set of circles.

clue.text: Mostly declaiming rubbish, as the doctor recommended?

indicators.note: rubbish signals that the letters are trashed and reassembled
mostly means all but the final letter is kept

explanation.surface: Talking mostly rubbish, as the doctor ordered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mostly' drops the last G of DECLAIMING; 'rubbish' rearranges the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Something taken for health on medical advice is curative, like a remedy prescribed by a physician.

clue.text: Writer held up by the Duke of Edinburgh

indicators.note: up in a down entry means the concealed letters read bottom to top
held means the letters sit concealed inside the title

explanation.surface: A writer is supported by Prince Philip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held' finds EOFED in 'dukE OF EDinburgh'; 'up' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Daniel Defoe wrote Robinson Crusoe, so he is an author.

clue.text: Literary doctor regularly phones about earlier unfinished work

indicators.note: earlier puts the shortened work in front
unfinished means the word for work loses its last letter

parts.note: a job is work

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of phones

parts.note: on means about, as in a book on birds

explanation.surface: A literary doctor phones regularly about an earlier piece left incomplete.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes H, N, S from 'phones'; 'unfinished' cuts JOB to JO, and 'earlier' puts it first.
explanation.definitionFit: Samuel Johnson, compiler of the 1755 Dictionary, is known as Dr Johnson, a man of letters.

clue.text: The way to remove dog's head

indicators.note: remove says a letter is taken off
head says the letter taken is the first

parts.note: a chow is a breed of dog

explanation.surface: Instructions for decapitating a dog.
explanation.definitionFit: How means the manner in which, as in 'that's how to do it'.

clue.text: Literary doctor inspiring us is an overweight American

indicators.note: inspiring literally means breathing in, so the word for overweight takes us inside

parts.note: fat means overweight

explanation.surface: A literary doctor who inspires us is a stout American.
explanation.definitionFit: Doctor Faustus is Marlowe's scholar who sells his soul to the devil, a doctor of literature.

clue.text: Sheep in the Darwin area the last to be released

indicators.note: in places the sheep inside the abbreviation for the territory

parts.note: Darwin is the capital of Australia's Northern Territory, NT
ewes are female sheep

explanation.surface: Sheep in northern Australia are the last ones let out.
explanation.definitionFit: The most recently published item is the latest out, the freshest release.

clue.text: Recent cowpat said to be doctored

indicators.note: said signals that the phrase is to be heard, not read

parts.note: new means recent; a turd is a lump of dung, and a cowpat is one

explanation.surface: A fresh cowpat is said to have been tampered with.
explanation.definitionFit: A vet who doctors a pet castrates it, so doctored is a euphemism for sterilised.
